title: The memory budget does not bound a build's peak memory
body:
`turns` in `libsufr/src/build.rs` cuts the partitions into turns by charging `size_of::<W>() + 8` bytes per suffix against the budget, 12 bytes for a u32 build. That covers the suffixes and keys a turn gathers. A code reading, not a measurement, finds more held during the sort: `sort_partition` builds a `Vec<(u64, W)>` of 16 bytes a suffix while the gathered vectors are alive, then the partition's suffix and LCP arrays, and `order_ties` copies each tie run. A partition larger than the budget gets a turn of its own. `--help` and `CHANGELOG.md` describe the budget as the most bytes of suffixes held in memory while sorting.

Jeb accepted the higher peak memory of the merged build on 2026-11-13: 12.0 GB against 9.6 GB for dev 657e16d on hg38 at 32 threads. This issue is about what the flag promises, not that figure.

## Options

- Charge the real cost per suffix in `turns`, so the budget bounds what the sort holds.
- Describe the budget in `--help` and `CHANGELOG.md` as what it counts, and say that peak memory runs above it.
